summary: Paraguayan general Alfredo Stroessner seized power in a 1954 coup and ruled for 35 years with US backing, running a torture police state, sheltering Nazi fugitives and abusing young girls before his 1989 ouster.

evidence.note: host frames the Triple Alliance war as scene-setting background, not the story proper
Stroessner introduced as a mortar commander in the Chaco War; parents and youth
1954 coup launched during a Philharmonic concert
1989 coup by son-in-law Rodriguez; exile in Brazil until death at 93
Odessa ratline, Rudel friendship and passports sold to Nazi fugitives
Pastor Coronel and the secret police; documented torture and killings
US aid and CIA trainers teaching torture to the regime's police
regime procured young girls for the dictator; 1977 Washington Post exposure
dissident doctors flee to Brazil and Argentina; abduction and torture in Buenos Aires
Stroessner's artillery wins the 1947 civil war; takes part in several later coups

notes: Part 1 spends roughly 15 minutes on 19th-century background (Francia, Solano Lopez, War of the Triple Alliance, Forster's colony); treated as scene-setting, so covered_span follows Stroessner's lifetime. Pastor Coronel's 2000 death year is from general knowledge. No theme for land inequality and patronage corruption.
